description: Cross-section rubrics for 4-category proposal quality evaluation. Core 7 dimensions apply to all categories; category add-ons provide category-specific checks.

core_dimensions.description: Proposal has sufficient sections with substantive content and covers RFP requirements

checks.description: At least 6 substantive sections present
No sections starting with 'Error:' or containing API error text
Proposal addresses the key requirements from the opportunity/RFP (budget, timeline, eligibility, deliverables)

core_dimensions.description: Numbers, names, and facts are consistent across sections

checks.description: Beneficiary count appears in 3+ sections and is the same value
Budget total in the budget section matches the amount mentioned in executive summary and other narrative sections

core_dimensions.description: Proposal uses concrete names, numbers, and locations rather than vague language

checks.description: At least 3 named locations (cities, districts, states, or specific venues) are mentioned across the proposal
Beneficiary counts, budget amounts, and timelines use specific numbers, not vague terms like 'many', 'several', 'various'
2 or fewer hollow phrases ('holistic approach', 'sustainable impact', 'transformative change', 'paradigm shift', 'cutting-edge') without concrete details

core_dimensions.description: Clear theory of change with measurable outcomes linked to activities

checks.description: A Theory of Change (ToC) or logical framework is present, either as narrative or structured (inputs → activities → outputs → outcomes → impact)
At least 3 measurable outcomes with indicators (e.g., '80% of participants will...', 'reduce X by Y%')
Activities described in the proposal logically lead to the stated outputs and outcomes

core_dimensions.description: Team capacity, timeline, and budget are realistic and aligned

checks.description: Team or staffing section mentions specific roles, qualifications, or existing capacity to deliver the project
Timeline/schedule is present and activities are reasonably distributed across the grant period
Budget amount is proportional to the scope of activities and number of beneficiaries described
80%+ of sections use first-person voice ('We', 'Our') rather than third-person ('The organization')
The funder is named explicitly in the proposal, not referred to generically as 'the funder' or 'the donor'
No unsupported superlatives or boastful claims ('we are the best', 'the largest', 'the first') without evidence

core_dimensions.description: Registration details present, no false claims about partnerships

checks.description: Organization registration number, FCRA status, or legal entity details are mentioned somewhere in the proposal
No claims of partnerships, endorsements, or affiliations that appear fabricated or unsupported by evidence

tech_accelerator.description: IBM-style product/tech grant — Suchi Cancer Bot

checks.description: Proposal clearly describes the current state of the product (MVP, beta, production) with specific metrics (users, sessions, uptime)
A deployment or scaling plan is present with infrastructure details (cloud provider, expected load, rollout phases)
AI safety, bias mitigation, or responsible AI considerations are addressed (guardrails, human-in-the-loop, data privacy)
User testing or validation methodology is described (pilot users, feedback loops, iteration cycles)
Technical architecture or system design is referenced (stack, integrations, data flow)

fellowship.description: Digital Minds-style leadership fellowship — Gautam Gauri

checks.description: Personal narrative has a clear arc: origin story, turning point, current mission, future vision
Writing feels authentic and personal, not generic or AI-generated. Contains specific anecdotes or experiences
Leadership growth is demonstrated through specific milestones, decisions, or challenges overcome
A learning or research agenda is articulated — what the fellow intends to explore, study, or develop during the fellowship
Track record is synthesized with specific outcomes (numbers served, programs launched, awards) rather than generic claims
Sections with word limits stay within +50% of target (e.g. 300-word section ≤ 450 words)
No sections start with org name or use 'We' as sentence subject — this is a personal fellowship application
At least 2 sections contain specific personal anecdotes — named events, people, dates, or moments that only the applicant would know
No two sections share more than 30% of their 3-gram tokens
Writing reads like a personal fellowship essay, not an organizational grant proposal. No budget justifications, Theory of Change frameworks, or deliverable tables.
No budget, INR, Rs, lakhs, fund allocation, or financial planning language in any section
No unclosed {{MISSING:}} tags, empty [citation:] tokens, or template placeholders left in output

add.description: 80%+ of sections use singular first-person voice ('I', 'my', 'me') rather than org/plural voice

donor_chapter.description: Asha for Education-style community grant — Diksha KHEL

checks.description: Cost per beneficiary is calculated and stated explicitly (e.g., Rs X per child per year)
Staff-to-beneficiary ratios are mentioned (e.g., 1 coach per 30 children)
Implementation section describes daily/weekly activities with enough detail for a volunteer reviewer to understand
Past performance data with specific numbers (children served, completion rates, years of operation)
Financial transparency elements present (audit status, fund utilization reports, previous grant outcomes)

partnership_pitch.description: Naandi 'Sports for Life' alliance — Diksha (non-RFP, concept note + pitch email + pilot design)

checks.description: The rationale for partnering is clearly articulated — why these two organizations together, not separately
Value proposition is mutual — both parties gain something specific (reach, expertise, credibility, infrastructure)
An operating model or governance structure for the partnership is outlined (roles, decision-making, resource sharing)
Clear next steps are proposed with specific asks (meeting, pilot date, MOU timeline)
Tone is peer-to-peer, not supplicant — positions Diksha as an equal partner bringing unique capabilities
